page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance in the Tau T2D family powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, providing 4 vCPUs with a direct one-to-one mapping between virtual and physical CPU cores. System memory totals 16 GB RAM, resulting in a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per core. The instance includes no local NVMe SSD storage and contains no dedicated hardware GPUs. Standard instruction set support includes AVX2 vector extensions alongside hardware AES and SHA cryptographic accelerations.

Performance benchmark testing indicates strong single-core CPU compute capabilities, reaching the top performance tier in stress-ng single-thread tests. Multi-core performance across standard workloads, including Geekbench, PassMark CPU, and Redis SET operations, remains average relative to hardware class peers. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 48.77 GB/s, while uncached write bandwidth measures 34.91 GB/s. In contrast, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput register weaker benchmark outputs.

The dedicated physical core architecture provides execution predictability without hyperthreading overhead or resource contention across shared virtual threads. Lacking local ephemeral disks, the instance relies on attached network persistent storage. This hardware profile provides resource efficiency for scale-out web backends, containerized microservices, build nodes, and general compute jobs requiring consistent per-core execution.
